newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah edges up in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah edges up in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah edged up in slow late trading on Wednesday following reports of an expected October inflation rate of 0.4 percent and the central bank keeping the fixing rate unchanged, dealers said.
"The central bank decision to keep the fixing rate unchanged boosted sentiment on the rupiah and prompted some dollar selling," one U.S. bank dealer said.
The dealer, however, said the rises were limited due to relatively ample rupiah supply.
Bank Indonesia maintained its intervention rate at 2,327/2,519 and the conversion rate to 2,327/2,375.
Dealers said reports of a likely October inflation rate of 0.4 percent month-on-month did not have much impact on the market as it had been expected.
Indonesia's consumer price index declined 0.04 percent month-on-month in September, compared with a rise of 0.27 percent in August.
One large local bank dealer said rupiah liquidity was likely to remain ample until the share offering period of the state-owned Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) ends on November 7.
Spot rupiah was at 2,327.30/27.60, compared with an opening of 2,328.0/28.5. Tomorrow and today were at 2,327.00/27.40 and 2,327.30/27.50, respectively.
Dealers said the dollar-rupiah rate was expected to range between 2,327.75 and 2,328.5 on Thursday.
Overnight swap was at 0.15/0.20 and tom/next at 0.35/0.40.
One-month swap was at 15.75/16.00, two at 31.00/32.75, three at 49.00/49.75 and six at 95.50/95.75 points.
